business_scope.primary_industry_name: Accounts Receivable Factoring and Cross-Border Reverse Factoring

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: European Union law (Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Articles 49-55 and 63) — free movement of establishment and capital for entities from EU/EEA states, including Spain
Spain-China Bilateral Investment Treaty (in force 2008) — relevant for Chinese-source trade supply chain capital
Spain-China Double Taxation Agreement (in force 1992) — relevant for withholding-tax verification on cross-border reverse factoring cashflows

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo, as amended; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 1784/1996, de 19 de julio, Reglamento del Registro Mercantil; Directive (EU) 2015/849 and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5) as transposed; Registro de Titularidades Reales — created under art. 4.2 of Ley 10/2010 and developed by Real Decreto 304/2014 (arts. 7-21), subject to the operational criteria of the Registradores de España.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the valid passport or national identity document of each ultimate beneficial owner and statutory manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority / national civil registry of the UBO's country of residence; if issued to the UBO directly, a notarized certified copy taken by a licensed notary against the original
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; for non-Hague states, Consular Legalization through the Spanish Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificado de Vigencia of every corporate shareholder in the UBO chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or equivalent registered-chamber authority in the corporate shareholder's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; for non-Hague states, Spanish Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the articles of association / constitutional documents and latest audited financial statements of all intermediary corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company secretary / statutory auditor of the corporate shareholder; signature and origin certified by the competent companies registry or a notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille on the certified copy; Spanish Consular Legalization if the origin state is not a Hague member

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for pre-incorporation representations, filings and signature of the SL incorporation deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the jurisdiction where the appointing shareholder/representative is located
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille; Spanish Consular Legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds / source-of-wealth certificate for the UBO and corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank or deposit-taking financial institution maintaining the relevant account; countersigned by the bank's authorized signatory and, where applicable, certified by a notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (notarized certificate of bank signatory); Spanish Consular Legalization if required by the country of origin

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening under art. 10 Ley 10/2010 and art. 7 Real Decreto 304/2014. Required databases include: UN Consolidated Sanctions List; EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; Spanish national sanctions registry maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, EU and Cooperation; SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias) information notices; and OFAC SDN List where USD clearing is anticipated. All UBOs and directors must be screened as PEPs, including domestic Spanish PEPs and foreign PEPs, with a mandatory removal of PEP classification no earlier than 12 months after the person ceases to hold public office. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for PEPs, high-risk FATF jurisdictions, opaque ownership structures, and any unusual cross-border trade finance structure involving invoice discounting or reverse-factoring platforms.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) — online name reservation and issuance of the 'certificación negativa de denominación social' via the official website of the Registradores de España y Registro Mercantil Central (www.rmc.es), coordinated with the Ministry of Justice's 'Sistema de Gestión de Denominaciones Sociales'
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under art. 404 of Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010 (Ley de Sociedades de Capital) and art. 7 of Real Decreto 1784/1996, the corporate name must be lawfully drafted and distinct from any existing Spanish registered company. Names may be composed of fantasy words, corporate/industry references, or combinations thereof, and may be in Spanish, any co-official Spanish language, or a foreign language, provided they are expressed in Latin script and transliterated into the standard Spanish alphabet where necessary. The legal form suffix 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' or its abbreviation 'S.L.' must appear in every official document and cannot be omitted. The Registro Mercantil Central compares names after normalizing uppercase/lowercase, accent marks, punctuation, spaces, and conjunctions such as '&'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registro Mercantil Central issues a 'certificación positiva' (existing or confusingly similar name) or denies a requested token, the applicant may submit a written reconsideration to the RMC within one calendar month from the date of notification, attaching the prior application reference. The RMC must resolve within 15 working days. If the rejection is confirmed, the applicant may file a 'recurso de alzada' before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministry of Justice within one month of the reconsideration decision. The final ministry decision may be challenged before the Spanish Administrative-Contentious Courts (Jurisdicción Contencioso-Administrativa). During the entire appeal window, a fresh name reservation application for a different name may also be filed without prejudice; the denied name certificate does not maintain any priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is conditionally accepted for provisional commercial registration by the Mercantile Registry, but it cannot consist merely of a P.O. Box. For a Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada dedicated to trade supply-chain factoring and reverse factoring, SEPBLAC and the applicable AML/CFT framework require a physical office in Spain where the compliance officer (Representante ante el SEPBLAC), records, personnel, and operational systems are accessible. A virtual-only address creates a high risk of denial of the factoring-related license application, adverse commercial substance findings, tax residence challenges, and enhanced inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk is high: estimated 60-70% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by SEPBLAC or other authorized authorities within the first 24 months of activity, given the Medium_Risk_Enhanced AML classification assigned to the trade finance factoring scope. If a specialized factoring authorization or regulated payment-related license is obtained, the probability increases to approximately 75% within the first 12 months, particularly where cross-border invoice discounting or third-country UBOs are involved.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance — 'certificación negativa de denominación social' (online application and certificate)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official ministerial tariff; approximate EUR 20-30 per application

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation and statutes (escritura de constitución) for an SL with 3,000 EUR minimum share capital
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff (Arancel Notarial), scaled by share capital and deed length; market benchmark EUR 650-850

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First registration of the incorporation deed in the Provincial Mercantile Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial / Colegio de Registradores de España
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registry tariff under the unified Registradores' fee schedule; approximate EUR 180-250

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Application for provisional NIF (tax identification number) with the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT)
Apostille / consular legalization bundle for five UBO and corporate KYC documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice or designated apostille authority of the document origin state; Spanish Embassy or Consulate where consular legalization is needed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory apostille / consular legalization fees, per document; approximate USD 100-150 plus notary/certified copy costs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn translation (English to Spanish) of apostilled UBO corporate documents and articles of association
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traductor jurado) recognized by the Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated sworn translation fee per word/certificate; market benchmark USD 250-400

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration preparation and filing for the Registro de Titularidades Reales / compliance with art. 4 Ley 10/2010
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary for signature certification and Registro Mercantil/UBO registry filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee and registry fee; market benchmark USD 300-500 including compliance advice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / virtual physical address with mail handling and official service per year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party corporate service provider or commercial landlord in Spain
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial market rate; flexible virtual office packages range USD 500-1,200 per annum

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT compliance onboarding — PEP and sanctions screening databases, SEPBLAC registration, AML policy, and compliance officer retainer (pre-opening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External AML/CFT compliance advisory firm or software provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Commercial market benchmark; plan USD 1,000-1,500 for initial setup and one-year regulatory advisor retainer

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Spanish corporate legal advisory fee for pre-incorporation due diligence, drafting of by-laws, and representation before the Mercantile Registry and SEPBLAC
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish law firm / registered corporate attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for fixed-fee SL incorporation package plus UBO and AML review; typical range USD 1,200-1,800

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 19-30, 58-62, 78-83, 210-242, and 249-252; Royal Decree 1784/1996 approving the Mercantile Registry Regulations; Law 14/2013 and applicable electronic incorporation procedures.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The relevant provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial), with name-certification functions performed by the Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), together with the application for registration in the provincial Mercantile Registry and the company bylaws.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: A standard Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may be incorporated with minimum capital of EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. If capital is below EUR 3,000, statutory reserve and shareholder-liability safeguards apply until the company reaches EUR 3,000. A company professionally conducting factoring as a regulated financial-credit activity must obtain authorization as an Establecimiento Financiero de Crédito and generally maintain minimum share capital of EUR 5 million, fully paid in cash or qualifying assets, subject to the applicable prudential framework. Spain has no single fixed state incorporation filing fee denominated in USD; notarial, registry, name-certification, tax, translation, legalization, and professional charges are separate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company subscribe for and issue its entire authorized share capital in accordance with the incorporation deed, with each subscriber paying the amount required by law and the bylaws. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full Spanish address], with authority to change it within the statutory limits. RESOLVED, that [name] be appointed sole director, or, if applicable, that [names] be appointed members of the board of directors, each accepting office and declaring no legal incompatibility. RESOLVED, that the appointed officers may complete all registry, tax, banking, licensing, and beneficial-ownership filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), online name-reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to five proposed names, identify the incorporator or authorized representative, pay the applicable certificate charge, and obtain the negative name certificate. Reserve and use the name within the certificate validity period. A foreign applicant should provide a notarized power of attorney, with apostille or legalization and sworn Spanish translation where applicable.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney, if filed by an agent
Apostille or legalization and sworn translation for foreign documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected, submit an alternative name or corrected application. If the certificate contains an error, request rectification from the Central Mercantile Registry before execution of the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Foreign Tax Identifiers and Authenticate Corporate Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria), through the competent tax office or electronic filing channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain NIE or NIF identifiers for foreign individual or corporate shareholders, directors, and authorized representatives as required. Legalize or apostille foreign corporate extracts, powers of attorney, certificates of incumbency, and ultimate-beneficial-owner evidence, and provide sworn Spanish translations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of good standing or incumbency
Board authorization and power of attorney
Apostille or legalization and sworn Spanish translation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to an AEAT information request within the stated deadline, correct identity data, and resubmit through the competent tax office or authorized representative.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporating notary and, where used, the CIRCE/PAE electronic incorporation channel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the bylaws, corporate purpose, registered office, share capital, share allocation, management structure, accounting year, and transfer restrictions. Expressly assess whether the corporate purpose includes regulated financial-credit activity. Obtain shareholder and director approvals and prepare the public deed package.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct drafting inconsistencies identified by the notary, replace unavailable directors or powers, and reschedule execution before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Capital Account and Pay Subscribed Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution maintaining the temporary capital account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an account in the proposed company name, deposit the subscribed capital, and obtain a bank certificate identifying the company name, amount, date, and subscribers. For a regulated EFC, document the higher regulatory capital contribution and source of funds. Do not treat escrow funds as operational funds before incorporation and account activation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide enhanced KYC and source-of-funds evidence, amend account data, or use an alternative Spanish credit institution if onboarding is declined.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary public (Notario) selected by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Sign the public deed with the shareholders, directors, or duly empowered representatives. The notary verifies identity, capacity, powers, capital subscription, payment evidence, bylaws, beneficial ownership, and legal declarations. Foreign signatories may sign through an apostilled or legalized power of attorney accepted by the notary.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure notarial objections by supplying missing documents, correcting the deed, or executing a rectifying deed before registry presentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the Company with the Provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry for the registered office, through the notary or authorized electronic presenter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the authorized electronic copy or certified copy of the public deed, pay applicable registry charges, and monitor the registry entry. Registration creates the regular registered-company status of the SL. Obtain the registry certificate and updated company extract after entry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a qualification note, cure each defect within the statutory correction period, request reconsideration or appeal where justified, and re-present the corrected deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Tax, Beneficial-Ownership, and Accounting Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish Tax Agency, provincial Mercantile Registry, and applicable Social Security administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain the definitive NIF, file the commencement and census declarations, register applicable VAT and withholding obligations, legalize accounting books electronically through the Mercantile Registry, and maintain the beneficial-owner register. Register employees and the employer account before hiring personnel.
required_dossiers: Employer and employee details, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected tax forms, provide missing registry evidence, and submit amended census, NIF, or Social Security filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Financial-Credit Authorization for Professional Factoring
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise, following the prior supervisory process with the Bank of Spain (Banco de España)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing professional factoring or reverse-factoring activities that constitute lending or credit-financing business, apply for authorization as an Establecimiento Financiero de Crédito, unless a legal exemption or alternative authorization applies. Submit the business plan, governance structure, qualifying-holding information, management suitability evidence, internal-control framework, AML controls, risk policies, capital evidence, and outsourcing arrangements. Registration with the Bank of Spain is required before operations.
required_dossiers: IT, cybersecurity, outsourcing, and business-continuity policies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Answer supervisory queries within the prescribed deadline, submit a remedial package, request a hearing where available, and pursue administrative appeal or judicial review against a refusal. Do not commence regulated activity while authorization is pending.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Municipal Premises and Operational Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal town hall (Ayuntamiento) at the premises location and the relevant autonomous-community workplace authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For an office-based factoring business, verify whether a responsible declaration, prior communication, opening licence, or activity licence is required. Obtain premises compatibility, occupancy, fire-safety, accessibility, signage, and construction approvals where applicable. Register workplace arrangements and preventive-risk documentation before staff commence work.
required_dossiers: Architect or engineer certificate, if required
Responsible declaration or municipal licence application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct technical deficiencies, file supplementary documents, request inspection, and appeal or seek review of a municipal refusal under the applicable local procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: For regulated factoring, the Bank of Spain and the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise under the Establecimientos Financieros de Crédito framework. For premises, the relevant municipal Ayuntamiento and, where applicable, the competent autonomous-community industrial authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Authorization to operate as an Establecimiento Financiero de Crédito, including professional lending and factoring activities; separately, a municipal activity, opening, or responsible-declaration filing may be required for the physical office.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico), together with the competent autonomous-community environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally exempt from project-level EIA for an ordinary administrative office conducting factoring, with no industrial plant, production process, significant emissions, or hazardous-material storage. A site-specific environmental or municipal review may apply if the premises are materially altered or include regulated installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, process VOC, or manufacturing-emission threshold normally applies to a standard factoring office. The company must comply with municipal sewer rules, ordinary waste separation, electronic-waste and confidential-document disposal requirements, and any applicable hazardous-waste rules. Any generator, fuel system, data-centre cooling plant, or other regulated installation requires separate permits and technical compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain the applicable municipal fire-safety and opening clearance, maintain emergency exits, evacuation procedures, fire equipment, accessibility measures, and occupancy compliance, and obtain structural or load certification where construction or heavy equipment is introduced. Comply with Law 31/1995 on Occupational Risk Prevention, prepare risk assessments and emergency procedures, and document employee training and preventive services. No factory-specific industrial safety clearance is normally required for a conventional office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Sede Electrónica (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) obtains its definitive NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) from AEAT after notarial incorporation and registration in the Registro Mercantil, using form 036/037 and identifying a legal administrator. Non-resident foreign entities without a permanent establishment that undertake taxable operations in Spain must obtain a non-resident NIF through AEAT (form 036), file an application signed by a tax representative in Spain, and submit apostilled or legalized corporate registration documents, articles of incorporation, certificate of foreign tax residence, and a sworn Spanish translation of all relevant instruments. The AEAT will issue a definitive NIF once the officer verifies identity and Spanish fiscal address details.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a check-the-box regime. Spanish resident SLs are automatically treated as separate taxable entities subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades. Available elections include the consolidated corporate tax filing regime for 90%+ controlled groups, special transparency regimes for temporary joint ventures (UTE) and economic interest groupings (AIE), the reduced start-up corporation rate, IP Box partial exemption, and R&D tax credit special allocation. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD are mandatory and not elective; Spain has no elective hybrid anti-avoidance mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration de minimis threshold; a taxable person must register with AEAT before first taxable supply. For intra-EU distance sales, the optional One-Stop-Shop simplification threshold is EUR 10,000; exceeding that threshold requires Spanish VAT registration or OSS reporting in the Member State of establishment.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time VAT information reporting applies under the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII) system for large taxpayers with turnover over EUR 6,000,000, VAT groups, and entities in the red/blue registration lists. The upcoming Veri*Factu regime (implementing Law 28/2022 and Crea y Crece) mandates B2B electronic invoicing with certified invoicing software, QR-linked digital verification code, and machine-readable invoice files submitted to AEAT through interoperable APIs. Exports and intra-community supplies must be reflected in customs declarations or periodic EU recapitulative statements.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export VAT exemption applies under article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law (Ley 37/1992) to goods dispatched or transported outside the EU by the seller, a purchaser established outside EU, or on behalf of either, provided the goods leave Spanish territory within 3 months or as evidenced by customs export documentation. Export-related services and services whose place of supply is located outside Spain under articles 69 and 70 LIVA may also be exempt, including reverse charge supplies and certain intermediary, transport, and ancillary services. The exporter must hold genuine documentary evidence that the goods physically departed Spain and the identity and non-resident status of the recipient.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo through the CUSTOMS TARIC declaration system)
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR consignment note evidencing physical export
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer documentation confirming settlement of the sale
Commercial invoice, packing list, and insurance certificate conforming with the export declaration
Proof of dispatch from Spanish warehouse or fiscal representative certification, where relevant
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT audits export exemptions by verifying DUA data, transport proofs, and payment flows. The failure to produce compliant export evidence within the statutory period results in retrospective VAT assessment on the full invoice amount, late payment interest, and a penalty base of 50% to 150% of the undeclared value-added tax under Articles 191-206 of the Ley General Tributaria. Where fraudulent zero-rating is shown, tax authority may file a criminal tax evasion complaint under Article 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code if the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000, carrying imprisonment from 2 to 6 years, fines, and loss of public benefits. Joint and several liability may attach to trading parties and professional advisers who knowingly participated in the false export arrangements.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting as the Eurosystem National Central Bank, together with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCIIN) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business for foreign-investment recording and FDI screening; the Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias (SEPBLAC) supervises AML/CTF countermeasures for the regulated sector.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain applies the eurozone's full liberalisation: the euro is freely convertible on both current and capital account, and no exchange-control licensing, surrender requirements, or approval is required for commercial or financial transfers (Law 19/2003, of 4 July, on the legal regime of capital movements and external economic transactions; Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union arts. 63–66; OECD Codes of Liberalisation). Profit remittance from a Spanish SL is unrestricted, subject only to: (i) corporate income tax compliance and the documentary burden for treaty-based dividend withholding relief (default 19% non-resident withholding; reduced rate available on submission of Form 210, tax-residence certificate, and UBO certification); and (ii) statistical declarations to Banco de España. The effective hurdles for a factoring entity are banking KYC/AML for the originator and the practical need to evidence beneficial ownership in the SL according to Law 10/2010.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is no statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds in Spain. Spanish exporters and their assignees (including a factoring company holding assigned export receivables) may maintain receipts in EUR or foreign currency, effect investment abroad, and repatriate funds without prior approval. Transactions of EUR 50,000 or more per operation are reportable to Banco de España for balance-of-payments and monetary statistics, using the Bank's operation-classifier codes; for direct-investment movements of EUR 3,005,060.52 or more, DGCIIN registration is obligatory, and non-EU FDI in sensitive sectors (e.g., defence, dual-use, critical infrastructure, media) remains subject to the RDL 34/2020 prior-authorisation regime.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (current account) + segregated factoring collections/escrow sub-account
Operational Account + capital escrow / disbursement sub-accounts
Operational Account integrated with Confirming/factoring settlement platform
Operational Account + trade finance (LC/guarantee) margin accounts
Operational Account + capital escrow for structured trade lines

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: LOW as the primary/sole liquidity host; MEDIUM as an ancillary collections or multi-currency wallet layer. Pursuant to Spanish Law 21/2011 on electronic money and the PSD2-derived regime (Royal Decree-Law 19/2017, Royal Decree 130/2019), only an electronic-money institution (EMI) or payment institution authorised or passported in the EEA may lawfully provide e-money, payment accounts, and payment services in Spain. An offshore digital EMI (post-Brexit UK EMI, US or LatAm fintech) that lacks EEA passporting rights has no regulated access to the Spanish market: it cannot open Spanish IBAN accounts, settle Spanish staff costs, or receive Spanish debtor collections with the same legal comfort as a credit institution. Such offshore EMIs may be used purely as a technical add-in via a contractual agency model with an EEA-authorised EMI/bank; they cannot confer the creditor-protection, factoring-escrow, or LC-issuance capabilities needed for a licensed trade-finance company.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, Spanish tier-1 banks require the physical or video-verified appearance of at least one statutory director (administrador) and the authorised signatories/MLRO. Law 10/2010, art. 3, mandates face-to-face customer identification unless the bank applies a qualified electronic-signature or an EBA-compliant video onboarding process. For a non-resident director of a Spanish SL, the bank typically additionally requests notarised power-of-attorney, apostille/legalisation, and, in many cases, an in-branch interview on Spanish soil before signing the treasury mandate. Remote-only onboarding is generally available only where the Resolution-Law 10/2010 conditions and the bank's own internal KYC policy permit EBA video identification and the corporate structure is transparent. For this Medium-Risk-Enhanced trade-finance/factoring SL, the prudent compliance posture is to plan a senior director trip to Madrid for board resolution signing, KYC interviews, and bank mandate execution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque UBO chain or nominee shareholding concealing the natural-person beneficiary of the factoring company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised certificate of the Libro Registro de Socios; updated Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) transcript; UBO self-declaration identifying all natural persons holding more than 25%; notarised powers of attorney; apostilled passport copies of shareholders and directors; Spanish tax-residence certificates; and audited financial statements evidencing the source of paid-in capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Duplicate or concurrent assignment of the same trade receivables ('double factoring' or non-verified reverse-factoring) creating layering risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Chronologically stamped receivables assignment register; debtor notification letters with acknowledgement receipts; registration with the Spanish factoring registry/association to evidence first-in-time assignment; certified invoice ledger tied to VAT/SII records; audit-confirmation circularisation to debtor accounts-payable departments; and legal opinions confirming absence of non-assignment clauses in the underlying supply contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned or high-risk counterparties appearing in the invoice chain or settlement instructions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated screening report covering EU consolidated financial-sanctions lists and OFAC SDN; passport/business-register extraction for each debtor and supplier; SWIFT MT199 bank-reference letters; jurisdiction-risk memorandum; full-chain trade documents (purchase orders, bills of lading, CMR waybills, customs declarations) proving the genuine movement of goods; and a contractual undertaking to cease funding upon any sanctions designation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party or split payments not matching the assigned invoice (indirect payment red flag).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written payment-direction letter from the debtor; assignment-notice clause in the factoring agreement; transactional matching output from the treasury workstation; proof-of-delivery, freight and customs documentation; debtor-side confirmation of accepted goods/services; and a dual-authorisation manual override protocol for any departure from the matched schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Invoice-financing for shell trading vehicles lacking operational substance and historic cash-flow track record.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Rental contract for registered office and warehouse; Spanish social-security and payroll records evidencing staff substance; audited financial statements for at least three years; AEAT tax-compliance and SII/VAT filing certificates; warehouse receipts, insurance certificates and inspection reports; and independent auditor or board-minute evidence of physical trade flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity injections into the Spanish SL should be routed as SWIFT MT103/ISO 20022 pacs.008 credits from the shareholder's bank to the SL's capital escrow account, with Remittance Information (field 70) stating the purpose—e.g., 'Aporte de capital social / liberación de capital' or 'Préstamo mercantil intragrupo'—and the beneficiary bank's classification code under Banco de España's balance-of-payments classifier. The incoming credit must be pre-flagged to the receiving bank to avoid statistical misclassification as trade payment. For inbound FDI, the DGCIIN declaration is required where the investment equals or exceeds EUR 3,005,060.52; non-EU residents investing in sensitive sectors (critical infrastructure, critical technology, media, defence/dual-use, or acquiring a 10%+ stake in a strategic listed company) are subject to prior-authorisation monitoring under RDL 34/2020. Supporting documents for bank release: shareholders' capital-increase deed (notarised and registered), registry certificate, a capital confirmation letter, and the agreed FDI declaration where applicable.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EU-disbursements (supplier payments under reverse factoring), use SEPA Credit Transfers (SCT, XML ISO 20022 pacs.008) settled in T2 real-time gross settlement; for non-EU/suppliers in foreign currency, use SWIFT MT103 wires with the unique end-to-end transaction reference (UETR) and appropriate Banco de España statistical purpose codes. For documentary trade, utilise SWIFT MT700/MT710 confirmed commercial letters of credit under UCP 600, or MT759/MT760 standby letters of credit and demand guarantees subject to URDG 758. Factoring and confirming receipts are settled by the factor to the supplier upon verified invoice and delivery data; the factor's bank should provide a segregated disbursement sub-ledger and a 'confirming' module to match assigned invoices, thereby preserving audit trail and preventing commingling of client money.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards (EUR/USD and EUR/LatAm crosses), executed under an ISDA/CSA or bank credit-line framework, with daily margin and settlement via CLS or correspondent clearing.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-currency exposures arising from debtor payments in Latin American and EMEA non-convertible currencies, cash-settled in EUR or USD.
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) to swap foreign-currency floating-rate factoring funding (e.g., USD asset-backed lines) into EUR, aligning funding and receivable currencies.
Vanilla FX options (EUR call/put combinations) to hedge downside on illiquid debtor portfolios while retaining upside; options may also be embedded in confirmed reverse-factoring structures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts, management report, proposed profit allocation, and beneficial ownership declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) of the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts approved within six months after financial year-end and filed within one month after approval; books legalized electronically within four months after year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in administrative fines generally ranging from approximately EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, increased up to EUR 300,000 for larger entities, and closure of the Commercial Registry sheet after one year of non-filing until compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Spanish State Tax Administration Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year; for a calendar-year company, normally 1 to 25 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment generally attracts interest and a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months; after 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus late-payment interest. Late or omitted filing penalties may also apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation and corporate register update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry and, where applicable, the Central Registry of Beneficial Ownership (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Beneficial ownership information is confirmed through the annual accounts filing where required and updated promptly following any change in ownership or control; shareholder and director registers must be updated contemporaneously with corporate changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated beneficial ownership information may prevent filing acceptance, trigger registry or AML compliance measures, and expose the company and responsible officers to administrative sanctions under Spanish AML and company-law rules.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT and withholding information returns, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Deadlines vary by form and activity, commonly January for prior-year annual information returns; Modelo 347 is generally filed during February, subject to current tax-calendar rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, incomplete, or omitted information returns may incur fixed or percentage-based tax penalties, with increased exposure where tax underpayment, inaccurate reporting, or repeated non-compliance is involved.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial and prudential reporting for a licensed factoring or financial-credit institution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Bank of Spain (Banco de España), where the entity is authorized or supervised as an establishment of financial credit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Periodic and annual returns follow the reporting calendar and templates prescribed by the Bank of Spain and applicable supervisory regulations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Supervisory breaches may result in corrective measures, reporting directions, monetary sanctions, management-liability consequences, and suspension or withdrawal of authorization in serious or repeated cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is generally mandatory where the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds for two consecutive financial years: total assets of EUR 2.85 million, annual net turnover of EUR 5.7 million, or average workforce of 50 employees. Audit is also required for certain regulated, supervised, public-interest, or specially regulated entities, including cases arising from financial-sector authorization rules.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General de Contabilidad) and applicable Spanish commercial-accounting regulations; IFRS may apply where legally permitted or required, particularly for regulated groups or consolidated accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must maintain accurate beneficial ownership and control information, update it following any ownership or control change, and provide the applicable beneficial ownership declaration with the annual accounts filing. Transfers of shares in an SL must be recorded in the Register of Members and reflected in the beneficial ownership analysis where control changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors and authorized representatives
Minute Book of shareholders' and management-body resolutions
Register of contracts with the sole shareholder, where applicable
Beneficial ownership records and supporting identification documentation

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 325-1,300 per year, excluding special mail handling, nominee, accounting, tax, or regulated-activity services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-10,000 for a standard SL audit; approximately USD 10,000-30,000 or more for a regulated factoring or financial-credit institution with prudential reporting and enhanced compliance requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general rate for Spanish resident companies. Newly incorporated entities may apply 15% during the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory eligibility and anti-abuse rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying newly incorporated entities: 15% rate for the first profitable period and the following period. Qualifying small entities may benefit from reduced rates or tax incentives under applicable annual legislation. Innovation, research and development, investment, employment and audiovisual incentives may reduce the effective burden where statutory conditions are met. Groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 750 million may be subject to the 15% global minimum tax regime.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: No statutory expiry period. Spanish tax losses may generally be carried forward indefinitely, subject to utilization limits, ownership-change restrictions, anti-abuse rules and the applicable tax base limitation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Corporate Income Tax return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades), filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic headquarters using an electronic certificate or equivalent authorized identification.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax year. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the standard deadline is 25 July.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number, registered address, tax period dates, entity type and filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Spanish SL is resident if incorporated under Spanish law or managed and controlled from Spain. Non-resident shareholders are reported as ownership information and do not convert the SL into a non-resident taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss under Spanish statutory accounts before corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include all accounting income and expenses of the Spanish entity, including cross-border factoring income, financing costs, foreign-exchange results and related-party charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary additions or deductions required to reconcile accounting profit with the Spanish corporate tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review interest limitation, impairment deductions, provisions, non-deductible expenses, withholding taxes, exempt income, transfer-pricing adjustments and expenses lacking business purpose.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions with related parties, including shareholder loans, guarantees, receivables purchases, servicing arrangements, management fees, technology, and treasury services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use arm's-length amounts and identify the foreign counterparty, jurisdiction, transaction category, valuation method and supporting documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening losses, utilized losses, generated losses and closing losses, subject to statutory percentage limitations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss utilization may generally be limited to 70% of the positive tax base, with a EUR 1 million minimum offset, subject to lower limits for larger turnover taxpayers and group-specific rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research and development, technological innovation, employment, investment, double-taxation and other qualifying credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credits require contemporaneous evidence, qualifying expenditure analysis and, where applicable, certification or formal supporting reports.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax base, rate and gross liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base after adjustments and loss utilization, applicable rate, gross corporate tax and applicable minimum-tax calculations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% standard rate unless the SL qualifies for the 15% newly incorporated-entity rate or another statutory regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payments on account and tax withheld
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Three advance corporate tax payments, Spanish withholding credits and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile Modelo 202 payments, domestic withholding certificates and legally available foreign tax credits. Do not claim foreign tax credits without proof of foreign tax paid and income attribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final balance after credits, withholding and payments on account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be made through approved AEAT payment channels. Refund claims require a valid Spanish bank account or an accepted cross-border payment arrangement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized electronic filing, payment reference and official submission receipt.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain the electronic filing receipt, payment NRC, accounting records and working papers for the statutory assessment period, generally four years subject to interruption and extended documentation periods.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with no tax due may attract a fixed penalty generally reduced for voluntary filing without prior notice. Late filing with tax due may attract a surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each additional complete month of delay during the first 12 months; after 12 months, a 15% surcharge plus late-payment interest generally applies. Formal tax violations may attract penalties ranging from 50% to 150% of unpaid tax, subject to aggravating, conformity and prompt-payment adjustments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax payments on account, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 1 to 20 April, October and December. The deadline moves to the next business day where applicable. Mandatory filing generally applies where the preceding tax period's net turnover exceeded EUR 6 million, with additional rules for consolidated groups.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish tax identification number, legal name, tax period and payment installment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's own identification number; foreign shareholders are not substituted for the Spanish taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-period tax liability method or current-period tax base method, depending on the regime selected or required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Factoring income, accrued interest, fee income, impairment and related-party financing must be reflected consistently with the selected calculation method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount payable on account of the current year's corporate income tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the installment with the Modelo 200 liability and prevent duplicate crediting or omission of prior installments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to make an installment may create a tax debt, late-payment surcharges and interest. Incorrect or incomplete reporting may trigger formal penalties and, where underpayment is involved, tax-base or tax-payment penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, informative return for related-party transactions and transactions with jurisdictions classified as non-cooperative or tax-risk jurisdictions, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the ordinary filing window is November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Counterparty, country, relationship basis, transaction type, aggregate amount and valuation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report cross-border related-party receivables purchases, shareholder or group financing, guarantees, servicing fees, software or licensing fees and management charges where thresholds are met.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts by transaction category and counterparty, including financing, services, royalties and asset transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use gross transaction amounts where required and reconcile them to the general ledger, statutory accounts and transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions or holdings involving jurisdictions included in the applicable Spanish non-cooperative-jurisdiction framework.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Escalate all payments, accounts, entities and beneficial owners connected to listed jurisdictions for enhanced tax, AML and substance review.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or filing inaccurate information may result in specific informative-return penalties, commonly calculated by missing or incorrect data, subject to statutory minimums and maximums, and may trigger transfer-pricing audit adjustments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 296, annual informative return for amounts paid and withholdings relating to non-residents, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during the first month of the calendar year following the year of payment, with the exact deadline determined by the AEAT filing calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident recipient name, tax residence, foreign tax number, address and beneficial-owner information where required.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain a current tax residence certificate before applying treaty relief or an EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, interest, royalties, technical services or other Spanish-source income paid or credited.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify factoring-related interest, servicing fees, guarantee fees and royalties according to Spanish domestic law and the applicable treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic rate, treaty rate or exemption code and tax withheld.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain the treaty residence certificate, beneficial-ownership evidence, eligibility statements and anti-abuse analysis supporting any reduced rate or exemption.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late, incomplete or inaccurate withholding information may generate informative-return penalties and does not eliminate the payer's obligation to recover unpaid withholding tax, interest and applicable surcharges.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding tax on dividends paid by a Spanish resident company, subject to domestic exemptions and treaty reductions. Dividends to a qualifying EU parent may be exempt under the Parent-Subsidiary regime where the parent holds at least 10% of the Spanish subsidiary, satisfies the minimum holding-period and subject-to-tax requirements, and the anti-abuse conditions are met.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence from the recipient's tax authority before payment, verify beneficial ownership and treaty eligibility, test principal-purpose and anti-abuse provisions, apply the treaty rate at source where legally supported, file the relevant withholding and annual information returns, and retain documentation. Where withholding was made at the domestic rate, the non-resident generally seeks a refund through the Spanish tax administration using the treaty certificate and payment evidence. A certificate of residence is commonly required to be current and may need renewal according to AEAT practice.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic Spanish non-resident income tax rates are generally 24% for non-residents outside the EU/EEA and 19% for qualifying EU/EEA residents for specified categories, including interest and royalties, subject to statutory conditions. Interest may be exempt for qualifying EU regulated financial institutions or under other specific domestic provisions. Royalties paid to a qualifying associated EU company may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive implementation where the ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax and anti-abuse conditions are satisfied. Applicable tax treaties commonly reduce interest and royalty withholding to rates ranging from 0% to 10%, but the relevant bilateral treaty must be checked transaction by transaction.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File documentation is generally required for related-party transactions exceeding EUR 250,000 in aggregate with the same related person or entity and within the same transaction type during the tax period, subject to statutory exclusions. Master File documentation is generally required for Spanish entities belonging to groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EUR 45 million. Documentation exemptions and simplified documentation for smaller taxpayers do not remove the arm's-length requirement.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods where the listed methods cannot reliably determine an arm's-length result
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not operate a separate regime formally titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless relevant under Spanish anti-abuse rules, beneficial-ownership requirements, the principal-purpose test, controlled foreign company rules, interest limitation rules, treaty interpretation and the general prohibition on simulation or tax-law abuse. A factoring SL should maintain Spanish decision-making, appropriate directors and personnel, risk control, systems, premises or operational capability, documented credit underwriting, servicing capacity, bank-account control, records and commercially supportable capital and financing arrangements. A conduit company with no genuine functions, assets, people or risk assumption may lose treaty benefits and face reassessment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and fraudulent return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing factoring income, fabricating receivables, understating taxable profits, deducting sham expenses or using false invoices with tax loss exceeding the criminal threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax fraud exceeding EUR 120,000 may constitute a criminal offense, generally punishable by imprisonment of one to five years and a fine of one to six times the defrauded amount. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or use of interposed entities, may attract imprisonment of two to six years and a fine of two to six times the defrauded amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur criminal liability where they knowingly participate, civil liability for restitution and tax debt, and administrative disqualification consequences. Travel restrictions or precautionary asset measures may be ordered in serious proceedings; imprisonment is not automatic and requires judicial determination.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting professional factoring, credit or financial intermediation activities requiring authorization without obtaining the appropriate Banco de España or Ministry authorization, or misrepresenting the entity as a regulated financial institution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory sanctions may include cessation orders, public censure, fines and other measures under the applicable financial-sector legislation. Where the business constitutes an establecimiento financiero de crédito, authorization, capital, governance, prudential, reporting and supervisory requirements apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may face administrative sanctions, civil liability for losses and, where conduct is fraudulent or unauthorized to a criminal degree, criminal prosecution. Personal sanctions depend on the specific regulatory statute and the director's involvement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using non-arm's-length interest rates, receivables purchase discounts, guarantee fees, servicing charges or group funding terms to shift profits out of Spain without reliable comparables or functional analysis.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may adjust the Spanish tax base, impose tax penalties generally calculated by reference to the unpaid tax or incorrect data, and apply interest. Failure to provide required documentation can trigger specific documentation penalties, commonly calculated per missing or incorrect item and subject to statutory limits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil or tax liability where they deliberately approve abusive arrangements, falsify records or obstruct inspection. Ordinary TP errors generally create corporate rather than automatic personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties or other Spanish-source income to foreign recipients without withholding, applying treaty relief without a residence certificate, or failing to file Models 216 and 296 where required.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish payer remains liable for unpaid withholding, late-payment interest and applicable tax penalties. Penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount depending on severity, concealment and fraudulent conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur subsidiary liability where statutory requirements for administrator liability are satisfied, particularly after failed collection from the company or where deliberate non-compliance is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, terrorist financing and suspicious transaction reporting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to identify customers and beneficial owners, accepting opaque receivables portfolios, ignoring sanctions screening, failing to report suspicious transactions to SEPBLAC, lacking a risk assessment, or allowing third-party escrow and SWIFT activity without transaction monitoring.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious violations may attract substantial corporate fines, potentially reaching millions of euros or statutory percentages of net worth, own funds or annual turnover, together with public disclosure, authorization consequences and management disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Members of the management body and compliance officers may be personally sanctioned where they consented to, enabled or negligently failed to prevent the breach. Criminal liability may arise for money laundering or terrorist financing, including imprisonment and asset confiscation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing fictitious receivables, recycling criminal proceeds through trade invoices, using controlled counterparties, or disguising illicit funds as factoring advances, repayments or settlement flows.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering may result in imprisonment, fines, confiscation of proceeds and instruments, and disqualification. Corporate criminal liability may apply where the offense is committed for the company's benefit due to deficient supervision or control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, beneficial owners and de facto managers may face imprisonment, fines, confiscation, civil restitution and precautionary travel or asset restrictions ordered by a court.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company, beneficial-owner concealment and tax residence abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using nominee directors, undisclosed shareholders, circular loans, artificial intercompany invoices or a foreign conduit to obtain treaty benefits without genuine commercial substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include denial of treaty benefits, recharacterization of transactions, corporate tax and withholding reassessments, interest, tax penalties and potential criminal tax or fraud proceedings.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners may face veil-piercing arguments, civil restitution, tax liability, disqualification and criminal liability where they intentionally concealed ownership or participated in fraudulent arrangements.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording nonexistent invoices, double-pledging receivables, altering debtor confirmations, hiding defaults or presenting purchased receivables as owned assets when legally transferred or economically controlled by another party.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential consequences include accounting and corporate fraud prosecution, contractual rescission, creditor claims, damages, confiscation and tax reassessment. Criminal penalties depend on the offense and loss amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur personal criminal and civil liability, including restitution to creditors, disqualification from management, asset preservation measures and imprisonment where statutory elements are proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Interest limitation and unlawful financing deductions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Excessive related-party debt, circular funding, deducting non-business interest, capitalizing shareholder advances as debt without commercial basis, or using back-to-back loans to extract Spanish profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowed deductions, tax-base increases, withholding reassessments, late-payment interest and tax penalties may apply. Anti-abuse, debt-equity and transfer-pricing rules may recharacterize the arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability is not automatic but may arise for intentional tax fraud, fraudulent insolvency, asset stripping or knowing approval of sham financing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Financing invoices, debtors, suppliers or shipping flows involving sanctioned persons, embargoed jurisdictions or prohibited goods without screening and escalation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, transaction blocking, license restrictions, asset freezes and criminal penalties may apply under EU and Spanish sanctions legislation. The exact consequence depends on the applicable sanctions regime and conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance personnel may face personal administrative or criminal exposure for knowing participation, willful blindness or grossly deficient controls. Asset and travel restrictions may be imposed by competent authorities or courts.
